910.name: Pre-Columbian Nicaragua
910.description: Early habitation around the great lakes, Chibchan and Mesoamerican cultural influences, Acahualinca footprints.

sub_clusters.name: Acahualinca Footprints
sub_clusters.description: Ancient human footprints preserved in volcanic mud near Lake Managua, earliest evidence of habitation.

sub_clusters.name: Nicarao and Chorotega Peoples
sub_clusters.description: Nahua-speaking Nicarao and Oto-Manguean Chorotega peoples in western Nicaragua, Mesoamerican cultural traits.

sub_clusters.name: Chibchan and Eastern Peoples
sub_clusters.description: Matagalpa, Sumo (Mayangna), Rama, and Miskitu peoples of the Caribbean lowlands and central highlands.

920.name: Statuary and Chiefdoms
920.description: Zapatera and Ometepe Island statuary, complex chiefdoms, regional trade networks, pre-contact societies.

sub_clusters.name: Zapatera and Ometepe Statuary
sub_clusters.description: Monumental basalt sculptures of human-animal alter-egos, ceremonial sites on Lake Nicaragua islands.

sub_clusters.name: Cacique Nicarao and Contact-Period Chiefdoms
sub_clusters.description: Cacique Nicarao's encounter with Gil González Dávila, philosophical dialogue, Spanish naming of 'Nicaragua'.

930.name: Spanish Conquest and Colonial Nicaragua
930.description: González Dávila and Pedrarias, León and Granada rivalry, slave raids, colonial marginalisation.

sub_clusters.name: Conquest and Indigenous Slave Trade
sub_clusters.description: Pedrarias Dávila conquers Nicaragua, massive slave exports to Panama/Peru, demographic catastrophe.

sub_clusters.name: León–Granada Rivalry
sub_clusters.description: Foundational liberal-conservative geographic divide: liberal León vs. conservative Granada, shaping national politics.

sub_clusters.name: Miskito Kingdom and British Alliance
sub_clusters.description: Miskito Kingdom allied with Britain, Mosquito Coast autonomy, trade, African-Indigenous mixing, resistance to Spanish control.

940.name: Independence and Walker Filibuster
940.description: Independence, federation era, chronic civil war, William Walker's filibuster takeover.

sub_clusters.name: Independence and Federation
sub_clusters.description: Independence (1821), Central American federation, León-Granada factional wars.

sub_clusters.name: William Walker's Filibuster
sub_clusters.description: American adventurer seizes power, declares himself president, legalises slavery, Central American coalition expels him.

940.name: Zelaya Liberal Era
940.description: José Santos Zelaya's liberal dictatorship: modernisation, canal negotiations, US opposition.

sub_clusters.name: Zelaya's Modernisation
sub_clusters.description: Secularisation, coffee expansion, railway, telegraph, Atlantic coast incorporation, canal ambitions.

sub_clusters.name: US Intervention and Zelaya's Overthrow
sub_clusters.description: Knox Note, US supports conservative revolt, Zelaya exiled, Dollar Diplomacy, beginning of US occupation.

950.name: US Occupation and Sandino Resistance
950.description: US Marines occupation, Augusto César Sandino's guerrilla resistance, creation of National Guard.

sub_clusters.name: US Marines Occupation
sub_clusters.description: Intermittent Marine presence, Dollar Diplomacy, Bryan-Chamorro Treaty (1914), client state management.

sub_clusters.name: Sandino's Guerrilla War
sub_clusters.description: Augusto Sandino wages guerrilla campaign against US occupation, 'General of Free Men', international symbol.

sub_clusters.name: Sandino's Assassination
sub_clusters.description: Somoza García orders Sandino's murder, eliminates rival, consolidates National Guard power.

950.name: Somoza Dynasty
950.description: Three Somozas rule Nicaragua as family fiefdom: land accumulation, repression, US Cold War alliance.

sub_clusters.name: Anastasio Somoza García
sub_clusters.description: First Somoza dictator, National Guard base, massive land acquisition, 'our son of a bitch' US alliance.

sub_clusters.name: Luis and Anastasio Somoza Debayle
sub_clusters.description: Dynasty continues, 1972 earthquake embezzlement, Chamorro assassination (1978), growing opposition.

sub_clusters.name: FSLN Formation and Insurrection
sub_clusters.description: Carlos Fonseca founds Sandinista Front (FSLN), urban insurrection, final offensive topples Somoza (July 1979).

960.name: Sandinista Revolution and Contra War
960.description: Revolutionary government, literacy campaign, agrarian reform, US-backed Contra War, economic devastation.

sub_clusters.name: Sandinista Revolutionary Government
sub_clusters.description: Literacy crusade (1980), land reform, nationalisation, health campaigns, Cuban and Soviet links.

sub_clusters.name: Contra War
sub_clusters.description: CIA-funded Contras operate from Honduras, Iran-Contra affair, 30,000 killed, economic embargo.

sub_clusters.name: Esquipulas Peace and 1990 Election
sub_clusters.description: Arias peace plan, Sapoa ceasefire, 1990 election — Violeta Chamorro defeats Ortega, peaceful transition.

960.name: Post-Sandinista Transition
960.description: Chamorro reconciliation, Alemán-Ortega pact, neoliberal reforms, Hurricane Mitch, Ortega's return.

sub_clusters.name: Chamorro Reconciliation Government
sub_clusters.description: Contra demobilisation, reconciliation, property disputes, military downsizing, economic stabilisation.

sub_clusters.name: Alemán and Bolaños Era
sub_clusters.description: Alemán massive corruption, Ortega pact, Bolaños anti-corruption, institutional weakening.

960.name: Ortega's Return and Authoritarian Turn
960.description: Daniel Ortega returns to power and consolidates authoritarian rule, 2018 protests, repression, exile.

sub_clusters.name: Ortega's Second Era
sub_clusters.description: Return via pact and plurality rules, constitutional amendments for re-election, canal concession to Chinese firm.

sub_clusters.name: April 2018 Uprising
sub_clusters.description: Nationwide protests over pension reform, 355+ killed in crackdown, student-led democratic movement crushed.

sub_clusters.name: Authoritarian Consolidation
sub_clusters.description: Opposition imprisoned, NGOs banned, bishops arrested, mass exile, 2021 sham election, international isolation.
